speaker: heba
text: Two shots. That's all it took.

speaker: heba
text: Ten past four that Friday morning, crouched behind my own bumper in a hospital garage, I learned what a life ending sounds like in concrete.

speaker: heba
text: I looked over the hood. A man was sliding down the side of a silver sedan, a gun a foot from his open hand. The man standing over him held a different gun, in his left hand. His right arm was in the plaster splint I had built thirty minutes earlier, in bay fourteen, with my own two hands.

speaker: lion
text: Go back inside, Dr. Marlowe. You were never here.

speaker: heba
text: I went back inside. Three days later, I married him.

speaker: heba
text: It started at 3:05 that morning, with a man walking into my ER holding his own arm closed. Half the waiting room went quiet for him. Denise at triage half stood up. The security guard found something interesting on his shoes. Everybody knew a rule about this man. Nobody had told me.

speaker: heba
text: Bay fourteen. A clean cut across the inside of his right forearm. Gray eyes. A thin white scar through his left eyebrow.

speaker: heba
text: "Knife?" I asked.

speaker: lion
text: I'd rather not say what cut it.

speaker: heba
text: "Somewhere you need to be?"

speaker: lion
text: You've done this before.

speaker: heba
text: "A couple hundred times. Usually on people who tell me their name."

speaker: lion
text: Nico.

speaker: lion
text: Vescari.

speaker: heba
text: By 3:40 I had built him a splint of plaster, fingertips to elbow. Six weeks, no gripping. If he grabbed anything hard, that tendon would snap like a rubber band. He set a fold of hundreds on my tray.

speaker: lion
text: For the chart. There doesn't need to be one.

speaker: heba
text: "There's always a chart." I tucked the money back into his pocket and typed his name while he watched. I said it too hard. He couldn't know why.

speaker: heba
text: Level two, spot 2-14. At 4:08 I found the charger in the cup holder. At 4:10, two shots went off, so close together they sounded like one word. I counted. One, two, three, four. Footsteps. Something heavy hitting a car door. At nine, I looked.

speaker: heba
text: "Let me get to him," I said. "I can—"

speaker: lion
text: He's gone, Dottoressa. Go.

speaker: heba
text: Behind him, in the stairwell, feet were going down fast. Then they stopped. Someone was standing on those stairs, listening, and those stairs were my only way out. I counted his breaths. Seven. Eight. Nine. Ten. The next one didn't come. The last time I stood that close to someone dying while other people decided I should stay out of the way, I was fourteen.

speaker: heba
text: At 4:16 I called 911 and my voice came out steady. By 4:31 the silver sedan was gone, and so was the man. The floor smelled like bleach and fake pine. The camera had been down since Tuesday. A young officer told me a car backfiring sounds like a cannon in concrete.

speaker: heba
text: I had a name on my tongue. I didn't say it. I'm not proud of that.

speaker: heba
text: Saturday at eight, a woman in a rain jacket and a man in a navy suit sat on my couch. Special Agent Reyes. Prosecutor Holloway. A city crew had pulled a man out of the Gowanus Canal. Frankie Lombardi. Two gunshot wounds to the chest. Frankie worked for the Vescari family, and also, quietly, for the FBI. That made his murder a federal case, and me its witness.

speaker: heba
text: I told them in order, like presenting a patient. Two shots at 4:10. Nico standing over a man by a silver car, a gun in his left hand, my splint on his right. Notice what I didn't say: that I saw anyone fire. I heard two shots. I saw what came after.

speaker: heba
text: Holloway left a subpoena. Thursday, ten a.m. He offered a new name, a new city, witness protection. I laughed. I had nine months of residency left. I wasn't becoming a dental hygienist in Tucson because a man in a nice suit told me to go back inside.

speaker: heba
text: "I'll tell them," I said. "But I'm doing it as myself."

speaker: heba
text: At seven that night I carried groceries up three flights and found my door unlocked and my lamp off. Nico Vescari sat in my mother's armchair in the dark, my splint resting on the arm. My little brother sat beside him, white as paper. "Ivy," Theo said. "I'm so sorry."

speaker: heba
text: Forty thousand dollars, a betting app, then interest. Theo was crying the way he did at fifteen, when he thought I couldn't hear through the wall.

speaker: lion
text: His bookie works for Carmine Brancato, who wants my port. If you die before Thursday, with my name in your statement, nobody needs a trial.

speaker: heba
text: "So someone wants me dead, and it isn't you."

speaker: lion
text: It isn't me.

speaker: heba
text: "Did you kill that man?"

speaker: lion
text: I'm not going to answer that.

speaker: lion
text: Marry me. A wife can't be forced to testify against her husband. The privilege belongs to the wife. Not to me. Not to Holloway.

speaker: heba
text: I laughed. "I met you on Friday. You bled on my shoes. Here's my answer." I held up the subpoena. "I'd rather testify."

speaker: heba
text: Sunday, a man in bay seventeen asked for the redheaded doctor. In the supply room the door clicked shut and IV tubing dropped over my head. You get about ten seconds before you pass out. I teach that to students. At five I drove my trauma shears into the back of his hand, and he ran.

speaker: heba
text: A huge man filled the doorway, the quiet one with the crossword. Rocco. "Go after him," I croaked.

speaker: heba
text: "No, ma'am. My job's you."

speaker: heba
text: That evening I stood by my car with a red line round my throat. I could become someone else in a city I'd never seen, or keep my work and my brother and trust a man I didn't. I was scared of him. I was more scared of a plastic tube. He answered on the first ring.

speaker: heba
text: "I have conditions," I said.

speaker: heba
text: His lawyer wrote it down in blue ink. One. I keep my residency, every shift. Two. My own bedroom, with a lock on my side. Three. Theo's debt, gone tonight. Four. No one in his family touches me, including his men. Five. When the case is dead, we divorce. Six. Not one cent of his money.

speaker: heba
text: "And seven. You never lie to me."

speaker: lion
text: I'll never lie to you. I won't always answer.

speaker: heba
text: "That's a loophole."

speaker: lion
text: That's the truth. You asked for the truth.

speaker: heba
text: "Is it the only reason you want this? If I can't testify, you're safe?"

speaker: lion
text: No.

speaker: heba
text: "What's the other one?"

speaker: heba
text: He held my eyes and said nothing at all. Beside him, Tommy looked at the table. Whatever it was, Tommy knew.

speaker: lion
text: My uncle Sal came at one-thirty with a box of cannoli and sugar on his tie. My father's brother, his consigliere for twenty-five years, and now mine.

speaker: lion
text: "You're a better man than your father was," Sal said. "But a better man makes trouble for himself. A girl in the house with a federal subpoena. It would be cleaner, Nico, the other way."

speaker: lion
text: We don't touch civilians. That's the only thing that makes us different from Brancato. Take that away and we're just men with guns who like the port.

speaker: lion
text: He held up both hands, cannoli in one. "I had to say it so you could say no. That's my job." Then he went out to the garden for air and left the door open behind him.

speaker: heba
text: Eleven pages, typed overnight. At the bottom of Nico's section, someone had added a line by hand in big, shaky, left-handed capitals. She will look like she loves me. I initialed it. I read every page twice.

speaker: heba
text: The ring was his grandmother's, a square emerald, far too big. It slid around my finger. "Rosa had big hands," he said. "She made bread."

speaker: heba
text: On the courthouse steps, eight reporters and three cameras. Holloway had been tipped. Nico kissed me, slow and warm, the plaster along my spine. It was for the cameras. For three seconds I forgot to count anything, and I was angry about that all day.

speaker: lion
text: Starting tonight, Dottoressa, we're in love.

speaker: heba
text: He had put a bolt on my side of the connecting door himself, at six that morning, left-handed. The screws were crooked. I tested it four times. The ring was so loose it kept turning to my palm.

speaker: heba
text: Tuesday, the ER. At work I couldn't wear a ring under gloves, so I'd threaded his grandmother's emerald onto a thin gold chain and tucked it under my scrubs. A wedding ring that lived against my breastbone. Joey, one of Nico's soldiers, rolled in stabbed, lung collapsing. I decompressed him and put in the tube myself while mobsters watched me do it. "Am I dead?" he asked. "Not on my shift."

speaker: heba
text: In his jacket I found my whole October. Every shift in blue ballpoint, small neat slanted handwriting I didn't know. And at the bottom, underlined twice: Level 2. Space 2-14.

speaker: heba
text: Joey said the man who sent him drove a car that smelled like anise. Only the hospital had my schedule. Dr. Bell had asked about my shifts that morning, almost casually. I told myself Bell asks everybody everything.

speaker: heba
text: I confronted Bell Thursday evening. He cried. His son Danny was seventeen and sick, and the treatment cost four hundred seventy thousand dollars. A man had asked about my schedule. Bell gave it. I gave him until noon to call the FBI. He asked for one more night. I said yes. I have thought about that yes every day since.

speaker: heba
text: That night I was shaking, and he held me, and he pulled the pen out of my hair with his left hand. I kissed him. He kissed me back. I stopped. No cameras. "That one wasn't for anyone," I said. "Sleep," he said. "I'll wake you at eleven."

speaker: heba
text: At 6:41 Friday morning, Priya called. Dr. Bell was dead in his Volvo, three spaces from my spot. A note on his phone. Suicide. "Ivy, I'm sorry. I couldn't live with it. Tell Danny I tried."

speaker: heba
text: In three years Bell called me Ivy maybe four times, always when someone had just died. In writing, always Marlowe, even in his last text. The note was a lie, and whoever wrote it didn't know him.

speaker: heba
text: Only four people had known he'd talk to the FBI at noon. Nico. Tommy. Rocco. And Nico's uncle Sal. When I said that name aloud, Nico's eyes dropped to the top drawer of his desk, for as long as it takes to read a clock.

speaker: heba
text: Sunday lunch under the fig. Enzo excused himself and didn't come back. I found him on his bathroom floor, blue, a foil card beside him. Oxycodone, thirty milligrams. I breathed for him. Two sprays of naloxone, three minutes apart. He gasped. I put the card in my cardigan pocket before the paramedics came. I only knew it mattered.

speaker: heba
text: In the ER, Enzo grabbed my sleeve and told me, because he thought he was dying. "I shot him. I shot Frankie."

speaker: heba
text: He had followed Frankie into the garage and stood half a flight up the stairs, holding his breath. A shoe scraped. Frankie turned, and his gun came up. Enzo fired twice and didn't even decide to. Nico took the gun out of his hand and told him to go.

speaker: heba
text: Enzo was the light jacket on the stairs. He had stopped when he heard me ask for a tube. Then he kept going. I told him what he said in that bay stays with me. I didn't know yet what it would cost.

speaker: heba
text: Then Theo was arrested. Four hundred tablets, taped under the driver's seat of his Civic. Holloway offered a trade: my testimony against Nico, and Theo walks. Nico, in the car, never raised his voice. "Do what you have to do. I won't hate you."

speaker: heba
text: I had my own evidence. The sticker on Enzo's card said Lot 4471-B. So did the pills in Theo's car. I cornered the hospital pharmacy director with an old committee letter. Forty-two cards of that lot had been "destroyed" on a form dated September twenty-ninth, co-signed by Dr. Marcus Bell. The tech said nobody counted. The signing doctor carried the bag out himself, past the garage.

speaker: heba
text: Nico's people found the dealer. His supplier was an old man in a gray Lincoln that smelled of licorice.

speaker: heba
text: Monday, Courtroom 6B. Holloway wanted the judge to call it a sham marriage. He called me to the stand and asked about the first week. About the courthouse kiss. And I invited him to ask the real question.

speaker: heba
text: "Do you love your husband?"

speaker: heba
text: "Yes. I love him. And I'd like the record to show he's hearing it for the first time with everyone else."

speaker: heba
text: The judge denied the motion from the bench. She'd seen a great many sham marriages, and none of them sounded like that. In the car, Nico's left hand lay open on the seat, palm up. I put mine in it. At my door he said, "One day, when you're ready, and not before, I'd like to hear it once without them."

speaker: heba
text: At midnight I couldn't sleep. Holloway had asked me that morning, "Eleven pages?" Only I, Nico, Mr. Feld and one copy in Nico's top drawer knew how many pages the contract had. Someone inside the house was talking to the government's side. I opened the drawer. Under the paper, a white twist of candy wrapper. It smelled of anise.

speaker: lion
text: One-ten in the morning, in my uncle's garage. I had found this car once before and told myself Brancato might be framing him. Half of Brooklyn sucks anise candy. This time I opened the glove box. A black ledger, its band off with my teeth because I only had one hand. C.B., every month for four years, starting the week of my father's funeral. And on the first of October: F.L. Twenty. Paid.

speaker: lion
text: In the trunk, a deli receipt for a prepaid phone, and a boy's tan jacket from a discount rack. When I was eleven, my father broke my nose, and Sal carried me out of that house.

speaker: lion
text: She was sitting in my study with the candy twist in her hand. I said it before she could. It's my uncle.

speaker: heba
text: At dawn, Danny Bell let me read his father's last letter. Marcus had signed the destruction form and carried the pills to a gray car for cash. Years ago he'd misdiagnosed a patient who turned out to be Brancato's cousin, and Brancato had held it over him ever since. The man in the gray car was old, soft-spoken, nice coat. The letter ended: Ivy, say it. Say all of it. Danny said I could give it to the FBI. I gave Reyes everything except one name. "Somebody else gets to tell you first," I said.

speaker: heba
text: Tuesday, seven p.m. Sal arrived exactly on time with a box of pastry. Nico laid out the notebook, the receipt, the jacket. Sal didn't blink. "Carmine wanted the port," he said, "and the port was you. Frankie lost his nerve. I didn't know about the stairs. I didn't know Carmine's boy would send Enzo down them."

speaker: heba
text: "Kids buy pills," he said. "Better ours, from a hospital, clean, than poison pressed in a bathtub in Jersey."

speaker: heba
text: I broke my own rule and spoke. "I breathed for your nephew for four minutes, Mr. Vescari. On your pills."

speaker: lion
text: My father would have put you in the water, Zio. That's the answer I'm not giving anymore. You'll go to Cefalù. Everything you own goes to Frankie's kids, Michael and Gina.

speaker: heba
text: Sal looked at his hands, then at his nephew. "Somebody in this family had to be his father. You were busy being a saint."

speaker: heba
text: I put my phone on the tablecloth and called Agent Reyes on speaker. Sal almost smiled. "Of course you called her, sweetheart. You always do."

speaker: heba
text: A day later I chained a deli receipt and a pack of gum to Paulie Ferraro. I called Reyes first, on purpose. Then Nico.

speaker: lion
text: Three weeks ago, I'd have sent Tommy. I trust what you'd do.

speaker: heba
text: Paulie confessed. Theo walked out at 12:52. In the car he said, "You never once asked me if I wanted to be your kid." I'd been so busy keeping him safe that I'd never asked. I asked.

speaker: heba
text: Monday night Lucia found Enzo's room empty. At 11:31 my phone rang. Carmine Brancato. His own son had overdosed on the floor of his club, and Enzo, who'd walked in to offer himself for a boy he'd hit on a bicycle four years ago, had asked for the doctor. I didn't ask permission. I told everyone before, not after. I texted Reyes. I went.

speaker: heba
text: Enzo was already breathing for him. I gave naloxone and bagged him. Four minutes twenty seconds. The boy coughed. Brancato took a typed statement out of his cardigan. I, Enzo Vescari, state that my brother ordered me to. Enzo wouldn't sign it. "I'll sign what's true. I won't sign that."

speaker: lion
text: I'm not armed, Carmine. My wife doesn't like it.

speaker: heba
text: Six guns turned. I stepped in front of him. "Be quiet. It's my turn." I told Brancato what I'd tell a jury. His son was breathing because of me. If anyone fired, I would stand in a courtroom and say who. He said, "In my house, we don't point guns at the doctor." He told them to put them down.

speaker: heba
text: Reyes came through the front door two minutes later with a warrant. She arrested Carmine Brancato.

speaker: lion
text: I came in with nothing because you were in that room. That's the truth, Ivy.

speaker: lion
text: Enzo turned himself in at two-fourteen Tuesday morning. In the visiting room I said, I'm sorry I made you carry it, and I cried in front of a guard. Then I went to Holloway about the gun, buried in the planter on Van Brunt Street under the geraniums. I told Feld to draw an uncontested divorce and leave it on the hall table. She gets to choose once with nothing on the table. That means I don't ask.

speaker: heba
text: Thursday, third grand jury. I waived my privilege myself, that morning at six, for October third and nothing else. I told them what I saw. Two shots at 4:10. A man sliding down a silver car. A second gun near his open hand. Nico standing over him with a gun in his left hand, pointed at the floor, held wrong, and his right hand in my splint.

speaker: heba
text: "Did you see who fired?"

speaker: heba
text: "No. I heard two shots. I saw what was in his hands afterward."

speaker: heba
text: Holloway told us in the hallway there'd be no indictment for Frankie Lombardi: Enzo's statement, my testimony, Frankie's gun, the chart. Nico would plead to tampering with a gun. At two o'clock I took off the splint, six weeks less one day. His fist closed. All of it, even the ring finger I sewed. He looked at his own hand a long time.

speaker: lion
text: Thank you, Dr. Marlowe.

speaker: heba
text: That evening there was a cream envelope on the hall table. Term Five. Three stapled pages. He'd signed it with his right hand, slowly, like a man writing in a foreign language. I put the papers down and went upstairs.

speaker: heba
text: I didn't knock. "Here's the thing about the divorce," I said. "I haven't asked." I emptied my cardigan pockets onto his bed: Enzo's foil card, the pharmacy form, his note, Bell's envelope, a candy twist. Everything I'd carried through five weeks. I took the pen out of my hair. On page eleven, under his left-handed line, I wrote, She does. And under that: Term six. Nobody in this house is quiet anymore.

speaker: lion
text: Last March a woman buried her son from my house on Carroll Street. Rosaria Amato. She told me about a red-haired doctor at St. Brigid's who sat with her and told her the truth. She said your name twice. I read Marlowe on your badge, and I chose that emergency room. That was the other reason.

speaker: lion
text: I love you, Ivy. I've loved you since you put my money back in my pocket and typed my name anyway.

speaker: heba
text: April. The lemon trees came out of their burlap. "It's a lemon tree," Lucia said. "It's Sicilian. It lives out of spite. Like me." Theo has an apartment over a laundromat and comes for Saturday lunch and calls me Iv. Enzo is in a program upstate, a hundred forty-one days clean, writing to his mother on Sundays and to a boy named Anthony who hasn't answered yet. Sal's letters from Cefalù, Lucia burns unread. Danny Bell is back at school; an anonymous donor paid his treatment. When I asked, Nico said, "I'm not going to answer that," and smiled. I finish residency in June.

speaker: heba
text: Reyes came to the gate on the first warm Saturday. A motion from Brancato's lawyers had surfaced old files. Nico's father had been an FBI informant for years. Nico would read it in the Post by Friday.

speaker: heba
text: I did not wait. We don't do silence in this house anymore. It's in the contract. I climbed fourteen stairs, counting every one, to tell my husband the truth about his father. Two shots. That's all it took to start all of this. One yes, said out loud, is how it ended.
